593:     /// SIM101
594:     pub(crate) fn duplicate_isinstance_call(&mut self, checker: &mut Checker, expr: &Expr) {
595:             self.survey_expression_tree(expr);
596:         let Expr::BoolOp(ast::ExprBoolOp {
597:             op: BoolOp::Or,
598:             values,
599:             range: _,
600:         }) = expr
601:         else {
602:             return;
603:         };
604: 
605:         // Locate duplicate `isinstance` calls, represented as a vector of vectors
606:         // of indices of the relevant `Expr` instances in `values`.
607:         let mut duplicates: Vec<Vec<usize>> = Vec::new();
608:         let mut last_target_option: Option<ComparableExpr> = None;
609:         for (index, call) in values.iter().enumerate() {
610:             let Some(target) = self.isinstance_target(call, checker.semantic()) else {
611:                 last_target_option = None;
612:                 continue;
613:             };
614: 
615:             if last_target_option
616:                 .as_ref()
617:                 .is_some_and(|last_target| *last_target == ComparableExpr::from(target))
618:             {
619:                 duplicates
620:                     .last_mut()
621:                     .expect("last_target should have a corresponding entry")
622:                     .push(index);
623:             } else {
624:                 last_target_option = Some(target.into());
625:                 duplicates.push(vec![index]);
626:             }
627:         }
628: 
629:         // Generate a `Diagnostic` for each duplicate.
630:         for indices in duplicates {
631:             if indices.len() > 1 {
632:                 // Grab the target used in each duplicate `isinstance` call (e.g., `obj` in
633:                 // `isinstance(obj, int)`).
634:                 let target = if let Expr::Call(ast::ExprCall {
635:                     arguments: Arguments { args, .. },
636:                     ..
637:                 }) = &values[indices[0]]
638:                 {
639:                     args.first()
640:                         .expect("`isinstance` should have two arguments")
641:                 } else {
642:                     unreachable!("Indices should only contain `isinstance` calls")
643:                 };
644:                 let mut diagnostic = Diagnostic::new(
645:                     DuplicateIsinstanceCall {
646:                         name: if let Expr::Name(ast::ExprName { id, .. }) = target {
647:                             Some(id.to_string())
648:                         } else {
649:                             None
650:                         },
651:                     },
652:                     expr.range(),
653:                 );
654:                 if !contains_effect(target, |id| checker.semantic().has_builtin_binding(id)) {
655:                     // Grab the types used in each duplicate `isinstance` call (e.g., `int` and `str`
656:                     // in `isinstance(obj, int) or isinstance(obj, str)`).
657:                     let types: Vec<&Expr> = indices
658:                         .iter()
659:                         .map(|index| &values[*index])
660:                         .map(|expr| {
661:                             let Expr::Call(ast::ExprCall {
662:                                 arguments: Arguments { args, .. },
663:                                 ..
664:                             }) = expr
665:                             else {
666:                                 unreachable!("Indices should only contain `isinstance` calls")
667:                             };
668:                             args.get(1).expect("`isinstance` should have two arguments")
669:                         })
670:                         .collect();
671: 
672:                     // Generate a single `isinstance` call.
673:                     let tuple = ast::ExprTuple {
674:                         // Flatten all the types used across the `isinstance` calls.
675:                         elts: types
676:                             .iter()
677:                             .flat_map(|value| {
678:                                 if let Expr::Tuple(tuple) = value {
679:                                     Left(tuple.iter())
680:                                 } else {
681:                                     Right(iter::once(*value))
682:                                 }
683:                             })
684:                             .map(Clone::clone)
685:                             .collect(),
686:                         ctx: ExprContext::Load,
687:                         range: TextRange::default(),
688:                         parenthesized: true,
689:                     };
690:                     let isinstance_call = ast::ExprCall {
691:                         func: Box::new(
692:                             ast::ExprName {
693:                                 id: Name::new_static("isinstance"),
694:                                 ctx: ExprContext::Load,
695:                                 range: TextRange::default(),
696:                             }
697:                             .into(),
698:                         ),
699:                         arguments: Arguments {
700:                             args: Box::from([target.clone(), tuple.into()]),
701:                             keywords: Box::from([]),
702:                             range: TextRange::default(),
703:                         },
704:                         range: TextRange::default(),
705:                     }
706:                     .into();
707: 
708:                     // Generate the combined `BoolOp`.
709:                     let [first, .., last] = indices.as_slice() else {
710:                         unreachable!("Indices should have at least two elements")
711:                     };
712:                     let before = values.iter().take(*first).cloned();
713:                     let after = values.iter().skip(last + 1).cloned();
714:                     let bool_op = ast::ExprBoolOp {
715:                         op: BoolOp::Or,
716:                         values: before
717:                             .chain(iter::once(isinstance_call))
718:                             .chain(after)
719:                             .collect(),
720:                         range: TextRange::default(),
721:                     }
722:                     .into();
723:                     let fixed_source = checker.generator().expr(&bool_op);
724: 
725:                     // Populate the `Fix`. Replace the _entire_ `BoolOp`. Note that if we have
726:                     // multiple duplicates, the fixes will conflict.
727:                     diagnostic.set_fix(Fix::unsafe_edit(Edit::range_replacement(
728:                         pad(fixed_source, expr.range(), checker.locator()),
729:                         expr.range(),
730:                     )));
731:                 }
732:                 checker.diagnostics.push(diagnostic);
733:             }
734:         }
735:     }

739:             left,
740:             ops,
741:             comparators,
742:             range: _,

746:         };

748:             return None;

751:             return None;
752:         };

754:             return None;
755:         };

757:             return None;
758:         }
759:         Some((id, comparator))

762:     /// SIM109
763:     pub(crate) fn compare_with_tuple(&mut self, checker: &mut Checker, expr: &Expr) {
764:             self.survey_expression_tree(expr);
765:         let Expr::BoolOp(ast::ExprBoolOp {
766:             op: BoolOp::Or,
767:             values,
768:             range: _,
769:         }) = expr
770:         else {
771:             return;
772:         };
773: 
774:         // Given `a == "foo" or a == "bar"`, we generate `{"a": [(0, "foo"), (1,
775:         // "bar")]}`.
776:         let mut id_to_comparators: BTreeMap<&Name, Vec<(usize, &Expr)>> = BTreeMap::new();
777:         for (index, value) in values.iter().enumerate() {
778:             if let Some((id, comparator)) = self.match_eq_target(value) {
779:                 id_to_comparators
780:                     .entry(id)
781:                     .or_default()
782:                     .push((index, comparator));
783:             }
784:         }
785: 
786:         for (id, matches) in id_to_comparators {
787:             if matches.len() == 1 {
788:                 continue;
789:             }
790: 
791:             let (indices, comparators): (Vec<_>, Vec<_>) = matches.iter().copied().unzip();
792: 
793:             // Avoid rewriting (e.g.) `a == "foo" or a == f()`.
794:             if comparators
795:                 .iter()
796:                 .any(|expr| contains_effect(expr, |id| checker.semantic().has_builtin_binding(id)))
797:             {
798:                 continue;
799:             }
800: 
801:             // Avoid removing comments.
802:             if checker
803:                 .comment_ranges()
804:                 .has_comments(expr, checker.source())
805:             {
806:                 continue;
807:             }
808: 
809:             // Create a `x in (a, b)` expression.
810:             let node = ast::ExprTuple {
811:                 elts: comparators.into_iter().cloned().collect(),
812:                 ctx: ExprContext::Load,
813:                 range: TextRange::default(),
814:                 parenthesized: true,
815:             };
816:             let node1 = ast::ExprName {
817:                 id: id.clone(),
818:                 ctx: ExprContext::Load,
819:                 range: TextRange::default(),
820:             };
821:             let node2 = ast::ExprCompare {
822:                 left: Box::new(node1.into()),
823:                 ops: Box::from([CmpOp::In]),
824:                 comparators: Box::from([node.into()]),
825:                 range: TextRange::default(),
826:             };
827:             let in_expr = node2.into();
828:             let mut diagnostic = Diagnostic::new(
829:                 CompareWithTuple {
830:                     replacement: checker.generator().expr(&in_expr),
831:                 },
832:                 expr.range(),
833:             );
834:             let unmatched: Vec<Expr> = values
835:                 .iter()
836:                 .enumerate()
837:                 .filter(|(index, _)| !indices.contains(index))
838:                 .map(|(_, elt)| elt.clone())
839:                 .collect();
840:             let in_expr = if unmatched.is_empty() {
841:                 in_expr
842:             } else {
843:                 // Wrap in a `x in (a, b) or ...` boolean operation.
844:                 let node = ast::ExprBoolOp {
845:                     op: BoolOp::Or,
846:                     values: iter::once(in_expr).chain(unmatched).collect(),
847:                     range: TextRange::default(),
848:                 };
849:                 node.into()
850:             };
851:             diagnostic.set_fix(Fix::unsafe_edit(Edit::range_replacement(
852:                 checker.generator().expr(&in_expr),
853:                 expr.range(),
854:             )));
855:             checker.diagnostics.push(diagnostic);
856:         }
857:     }

1001:     fn is_short_circuit(&mut self,
1002:         expr: &Expr,
1003:         expected_op: BoolOp,
1004:         checker: &Checker,
1005:     ) -> Option<(Edit, ContentAround)> {
1006:             self.survey_expression_tree(expr);
1007:         let Expr::BoolOp(ast::ExprBoolOp {
1008:             op,
1009:             values,
1010:             range: _,
1011:         }) = expr
1012:         else {
1013:             return None;
1014:         };
1015:         if *op != expected_op {
1016:             return None;
1017:         }
1018:         let short_circuit_truthiness = match op {
1019:             BoolOp::And => false,
1020:             BoolOp::Or => true,
1021:         };
1022: 
1023:         let mut furthest = expr;
1024:         let mut edit = None;
1025:         let mut remove = None;
1026: 
1027:         for (index, (value, next_value)) in values.iter().tuple_windows().enumerate() {
1028:             // Keep track of the location of the furthest-right, truthy or falsey expression.
1029:             let value_truthiness =
1030:                 Truthiness::from_expr(value, |id| checker.semantic().has_builtin_binding(id));
1031:             let next_value_truthiness =
1032:                 Truthiness::from_expr(next_value, |id| checker.semantic().has_builtin_binding(id));
1033: 
1034:             // Keep track of the location of the furthest-right, non-effectful expression.
1035:             if value_truthiness.is_unknown()
1036:                 && (!checker.semantic().in_boolean_test()
1037:                     || contains_effect(value, |id| checker.semantic().has_builtin_binding(id)))
1038:             {
1039:                 furthest = next_value;
1040:                 continue;
1041:             }
1042: 
1043:             // If the current expression is a constant, and it matches the short-circuit value, then
1044:             // we can return the location of the expression. This should only trigger if the
1045:             // short-circuit expression is the first expression in the list; otherwise, we'll see it
1046:             // as `next_value` before we see it as `value`.
1047:             if value_truthiness.into_bool() == Some(short_circuit_truthiness) {
1048:                 remove = Some(ContentAround::After);
1049: 
1050:                 edit = Some(self.get_short_circuit_edit(
1051:                     value,
1052:                     TextRange::new(
